sprint_goal: PyYAML is required and checked at install, the installer fails safe, and the TRD and PRD describe the shipped code.

seats.achievable: yes - US1296 (install.sh/ps1 refuse without yaml), US1297 and US1298 (reader and gate refuse) make 'required and checked' true; BG1543/BG1546/BG1547 have failing-capable Verify lines for fail-safe. TRD/PRD clause is reachable only for the listed drift: 'describe the shipped code' overstates, since no unit sweeps for unlisted drift.
seats.done_means: Clause 1: PyYAML required, checked at install and by the code: US1296, US1297, US1298, US1299 AC1. Clause 2: installer fails safe: BG1543 (sidecar fault refuses), BG1546 (no false banner or exit 0), BG1547 (uninstall guard). Clause 3: TRD/PRD match code: US1299, BG1516/17/29/30/31/33/96, BG1556/57/65/1621, BG1525-28, BG1180, BG1553-55; BG1162/BG1168 guard against re-drift. Serves O4 (specs reconciled).
seats.one_increment: yes - every unit serves a clause; the doc bugs are one shared-file cluster, so they serialise but read as one increment. US1297/US1298 are the riskiest (high risk-class gate) and are code, not paperwork.
seats.note: Spec pages state PyYAML as required, install and gate refuse without it, installer fails safe, and the 21 listed spec drifts are fixed.

seats.achievable: yes, with a caveat - the PyYAML clause is reached by US1296-US1298 and US1299, the fails-safe clause by BG1543/BG1546/BG1547. The docs clause is reached only for the 18 named drifts (BG1516-BG1621); 'the TRD and PRD describe the shipped code' as an absolute overstates, since unlisted drift can remain.
seats.done_means: Clause 1: US1296 (both installers refuse without yaml), US1297 (config reader refuses), US1298 (gate commands exit non-zero), US1299 (standard-library-only claim dropped). Clause 2: BG1543 (fetch failure not read as no digest), BG1546 (no banner/exit 0 on refusal), BG1547 (uninstall identity guard). Clause 3: TRD bugs BG1516 BG1517 BG1529 BG1530 BG1531 BG1533 BG1096 BG1556 BG1557 BG1565 BG1621, PRD bugs BG1525-BG1528 BG1180 BG1553-BG1555. Serves O4 and Maya End goal 4 (specs never drift), Rowan End goal 2 (installed copy trustworthy).
seats.one_increment: mostly yes - two themes (installer safety, doc truth) joined by US1299 and the PyYAML claim. BG1162 and BG1168 strengthen PRD test machinery rather than describe shipped code; they serve no clause directly and read as a follow-up, though they guard clause 3 against re-drift.
seats.note: Goal: PyYAML is required and checked at install, the installer fails safe, and the named TRD and PRD drifts match shipped code.

seats.achievable: yes - US1296 (installers refuse without PyYAML), US1297 (config reader), US1298 (gate) carry executable Verify lines with negative cases, and the 11 TRD and 11 PRD bugs each name a specific wrong sentence. Caveat: 'describe the shipped code' is only as real as each doc claim being run (LC-018); a doc-only bug can go green by rewording.
seats.done_means: Clause 1 (required, checked at install): US1296 AC1-2, US1297, US1298, US1299 AC1 (no stdlib-only claim). Clause 2 (fails safe): BG1543 (fetch failure not read as no digest), BG1546 (all skipped must not exit 0), BG1547 (uninstall identity guard). Clause 3 (TRD/PRD true): TRD BG1516 BG1517 BG1529 BG1530 BG1531 BG1533 BG1096 BG1556 BG1557 BG1565 BG1621; PRD BG1525-1528 BG1162 BG1168 BG1180 BG1553-1555; US1299 AC2-3. Serves O4 (specs reconciled) and O1.
seats.one_increment: yes - every unit serves one of the three clauses. Clause 3 dominates at 22 of 28 units, a documentation sweep with no shared fix. BG1162 and BG1168 harden the PRD test, which is test-hardening rather than a clause, but they protect the PRD-accuracy clause.
